definitions.definition: For x∈ℝⁿ and r>0, e(x,r)=‖u_t(x,r)‖₂²+∑_{j=1}^n‖∂_{x_j}u(x,r)‖₂²; the vector norms are Euclidean, and the spatial-gradient term is the Frobenius/Hilbert–Schmidt square of the Jacobian.

definitions.type: positive integer k maps to Euclidean/Borel/Lebesgue measure space on ℝᵏ
definitions.definition: For each positive integer k, identify ℝᵏ with the finite product Fin k→ℝ, equip it with its Euclidean norm and topology, the Borel σ-algebra generated by that topology, and product Lebesgue measure (the product of one-dimensional Lebesgue volume on each coordinate).

inputs.statement: For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable. For every t>0 there exist a finite closed interval J=[s₀,s₁]⊂(0,∞) with s₀<t<s₁ and a compact set C⊂ℝⁿ such that, for every s∈J and x∉C, u(x,s)=q, ∂_s u(x,s)=0, and ∂_{x_j}u(x,s)=0 for every j∈Fin n; for every s∈J, the maps x↦u_t(x,s), x↦∂_{x_j}u(x,s), x↦e(x,s), and x↦e_t(x,s) are continuous on ℝⁿ and vanish for every x∉C, for each j∈Fin n. The ambient measurable space on ℝⁿ is the Borel σ-algebra generated by its Euclidean topology, and Lebesgue measure μ satisfies μ(K)<∞ for every compact K⊂ℝⁿ.
For each compact interval J⊂(0,∞), compact C_J exists with u=q outside C_J throughout J.
For topological spaces X,Y and compact subsets s⊆X,t⊆Y, the product s×t is compact.

output.statement: For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable. For every t>0 there exist a finite closed interval J=[s₀,s₁]⊂(0,∞) with s₀<t<s₁ and a compact set C⊂ℝⁿ such that, for every s∈J and x∉C, u(x,s)=q, ∂_s u(x,s)=0, and ∂_{x_j}u(x,s)=0 for every j∈Fin n; for every s∈J, the maps x↦u_t(x,s), x↦∂_{x_j}u(x,s), x↦e(x,s), and x↦e_t(x,s) are continuous on ℝⁿ and vanish for every x∉C, for each j∈Fin n. The ambient measurable space on ℝⁿ is the Borel σ-algebra generated by its Euclidean topology, and every compact K⊂ℝⁿ is Borel measurable with finite Lebesgue measure μ(K)<∞.

locals.declaration: Choose compact C from H003 for the time window J.

locals.type: nonnegative real bound for |e_t| on C*×J
locals.declaration: Choose a finite nonnegative real upper bound K from the bounded-above conclusion of M019.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary r>0, let J=[r/2,3r/2], choose compact C from H003, and define C*=C∪{0}. The set C* is compact and nonempty; outside C* we still have u=q throughout J. The function (x,τ)↦|e_t(x,τ)| is continuous on C*×J by smoothness, and C*×J is compact by M005. Apply M019; its bounded-above conclusion supplies a real upper bound, so choose a finite K≥0 with |e_t(x,τ)|≤K for all (x,τ)∈C*×J. Define b(x)=K·1_{C*}(x). Outside C*, e_t=0 by smoothness and constancy of u on the open spatial complement; hence |e_t(x,τ)|≤b(x) for every x and τ∈J. By N001 every compact set is measurable and has finite Lebesgue measure. M008 makes the constant K integrable on C*, and M009 makes b integrable on ℝⁿ. Define F(τ)(x)=e(x,τ) and Fprime(τ)(x)=e_t(x,τ). Smoothness implies strong measurability; N001 gives F(r) integrable and Fprime(r) strongly measurable. The interval (r/2,3r/2) is a neighborhood of r. The pointwise parameter derivative of F is Fprime by smoothness, and the bound by b holds for every x and every τ in this neighborhood. Thus M006 applies and yields differentiability of E at r with E′(r)=∫e_t(x,r)dx. Since r was arbitrary, the output follows.
